title: Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Stephen Smith
speeches.brief: Moved the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2013 implementing the Hawke review, creating a permit system to allow non-defence mining and resources access to the 127,000 square kilometre military testing range while defence remains the primary user, noting the South Australian government estimates about $35 billion in exploitable minerals within the area, and capped compensation for property loss at $2 million.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Gave the coalition's guarded support to the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2013, describing the 127,000 square kilometre testing range, the world's largest, as holding an estimated $35 billion in exploitable mineral resources over the next decade, while insisting defence must remain the area's primary use and seeking referral to a Senate committee.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: Opposed the rushed process behind the Defence Legislation Amendment (Woomera Prohibited Area) Bill 2013, noting traditional owners had only three working days to make submissions, warned the area holds an estimated 75 per cent of Australia's known uranium reserves, and highlighted that BHP already extracts up to 42 million litres of water a day for free at its nearby Roxby Downs mine.
